regions.region: page 1 title, abstract, author block, and SI availability statement
regions.finding: Confirmed the article title as 'The Renaissance of an Old Problem: Highly Regioselective Carboxylation of 2-Alkynyl Bromides with Carbon Dioxide' and DOI 10.1002/chem.201503494. The paper points to online Supporting Information, but no SI file was explicitly supplied or associated in this workspace; no SI facts were imported.

Classical allenoate/CO and In/Al/Ga carbonyl-addition routes are cited prior work; the new CO2/Zn primary-versus-secondary bromide transformation is a generic current reaction class. These are classified as one general overview, not experiment-specific rows.

The narrative identifies fourteen optimization outcomes: a complicated In run, Al/Bi/Mn failures with starting-material recovery, Zn product mixtures, solvent/additive/temperature effects, and the 65 °C >99:1 selectivity result. These map to the fourteen Table 1 records on page 2 rather than duplicate prose records.
The primary-bromide scope discussion maps to Table 2 entries on page 3. The distinct 100 mmol repeat of 1a is retained separately because its scale and staged operation differ from the 1 mmol run.

unresolved: The page-1 prose does not independently state row-wise workups, product masses, or analytical bases beyond the Table 1 NMR discussion.
SI association remains unestablished; all structure candidates remain machine-unverified.

regions.finding: The original image distinguishes cited classical routes (Scheme 1a/b) from the generic current CO2/Zn route (Scheme 1c), with primary bromides shown at 65 °C and secondary bromides at 20 °C. It is a general scheme, not a unique run.

regions.region: page 2 lower-left Table 1, entries 1–14 and footnotes a–c
regions.finding: Fourteen independent optimization experiments were read row-by-row. Shared 1a 1.0 mmol, additive 1.0 mmol, solvent 5 mL, CO2 balloon, 24 h, metal pretreatment, NMR basis, row metal loading/solvent/additive/temperature, product yields, recoveries, '<1', 'complicated', and all printed dashes were preserved.
Four distinct 2a derivatizations are introduced: benzyl allenoate 2aa, allenoyl amide 2ab, furanone 2ac, and pyrazolone 2ad. Their arrows/conditions/yields are read from page 3 and not collapsed.

regions.region: page 2 right-column Table 3 and Scheme 3 discussion
regions.finding: The secondary-bromide series gives 3-alkynoic acids with a series-level trace allenoic-acid statement; thirteen rows appear on page 3. The two KOH rearrangements to 4n and 4p are distinct later arrows.
The authors propose LiCl-solubilized organozinc species and alternative cyclic SE2′ pathways IM-1/IM-2; this maps to the Scheme 4 mechanism record and is not treated as preparation of intermediates.

unresolved: Table 1 dashes are undefined source markers and were not interpreted as zero.
The series-level trace allenoic-acid statement is not numerically or row-wise resolved.

regions.region: page 3 upper-left Table 2 and footnotes a–d
regions.finding: Eleven primary-bromide scope rows were read with shared Zn/LiCl/CO2/DME/65 °C/24 h conditions and isolated yields. Table entry 1 at 1 mmol is merged with the matching Table 1/detailed run; the parenthesized 100 mmol repeat is distinct. Entry 9's duplicated source label 1g versus product 2i is preserved as a conflict.

regions.region: page 3 upper-right Table 3 and footnotes a–d
regions.finding: Thirteen secondary-bromide scope rows were read independently with shared Zn/LiCl/CO2/DME/20 °C/24 h conditions; entry 12 alone is overridden to 65 °C. Isolated yields and the metal pretreatment footnote were structured.

Four independent arrows were retained: 2a→2aa (BnBr/K2CO3, acetone, room temperature, 96%), 2a→2ab (TsNCO/Et3N, THF, 70%), 2a→2ac (PdCl2 5 mol%, allyl bromide, DMA, 50 °C, 50%), and 2a→2ad (DEAD/Ph3P, DCM, 80%).
Two distinct KOH-mediated rearrangements were retained under KOH 10 equiv/MeOH reflux/12 h: 3n→4n (72%) and 3p→4p (70%).

regions.region: page 3 lower Experimental Section and 1 mmol 2a procedure
regions.finding: The detailed 1 mmol 1a→2a run was merged with Table 1 entry 13/Table 2 entry 1, adding exact Zn/LiCl/1a/DME charges, ordered Ar charging, liquid-N2 freezing/CO2 replacement/thawing, 65 °C/24 h hold, workup, chromatography, 99.5 mg/0.71 mmol, and 71% isolated yield. The page-3 drawing's 100 mmol label is assigned to the separate scale-up continued on page 4.

regions.region: page 3 bottom-right beginning of 100 mmol procedure
regions.finding: The distinct 100 mmol scale-up begins with Zn 6.87 g/105 mmol, LiCl 4.24 g/100 mmol, and DME 500 mL; it continues on page 4 and is represented once with cross-page evidence.

unresolved: Most scope rows omit workup, purification, isolated masses, and selectivity analytical bases.
Compact Scheme 2/3 products remain label-only where connectivity or stereochemistry was not encoded confidently.

regions.finding: The original diagram shows equilibrating propargyl/allenyl zinc species, IM-1/IM-2 cyclic transition states, zinc carboxylates, and acid workup. It is classified as mechanism; no intermediate is treated as an isolated preparation.

regions.region: page 4 left-column continuation of 100 mmol 2a experiment
regions.finding: Completes the scale-up record: 1a 17.51 g/100 mmol, Ar charging, liquid-N2 freezing and CO2 replacement, 65 °C for 12 h, new CO2 balloon, another 12 h, HCl/EtOAc/brine/Na2SO4 workup, chromatography, and 2a 9.96 g/71 mmol/71%.

Shangze Wu is thanked for reproducing Table 2 entry 3, Table 3 entry 4, and Scheme 2 product 2ad. No independent quantities, conditions, or run identifiers are supplied, so no duplicate experiments were created.
Bibliography/prior-literature context only. External papers were not expanded into current-paper experiments.
